events.title: Ruby on Rails open sourced
events.summary: David Heinemeier Hansson released Rails 0.5.0 — MVC infrastructure extracted from Basecamp.
events.about: Ruby on Rails is a web framework for database-backed sites — models, views, controllers out of the box. Used to ship CRUD apps fast: project tools (Basecamp), early Twitter/GitHub/Shopify, and countless startup MVPs. Convention over configuration means less boilerplate than hand-rolled PHP or Java servlets.

narrative.whyChosen: Rails popularized convention-over-configuration and made Ruby a global language for web startups.
narrative.whyImportant: Active Record and Action Pack became the template for modern full-stack web frameworks.
narrative.problemSolved: Building database-backed web apps required repetitive wiring; Rails packaged opinionated defaults.

events.title: PHP 5.0 released
events.summary: The PHP project released PHP 5.0 on July 13, 2004 with Zend Engine 2, objects, exceptions, and a redesigned object model.
events.about: PHP 5 turned PHP from a scripting language with classes bolted on into something closer to a real OOP language — constructors, destructors, visibility, interfaces, and exceptions. It powered the WordPress and Drupal boom and set the stage for PHP's dominance on shared hosting through the 2000s.

narrative.whyChosen: PHP 5 was the object-model rewrite that made PHP viable for frameworks and CMSs.
narrative.whyImportant: Exceptions and a proper object model replaced PHP 4's shallow class syntax.
narrative.problemSolved: PHP 4's object handling was too limited for growing web applications and frameworks.

events.title: Apache Maven 1.0 released
events.summary: The Apache Maven team released Maven 1.0 on July 13, 2004 — a Java build and project comprehension tool centered on the Project Object Model (POM).
events.about: Maven standardizes Java project layout, dependencies, and lifecycle phases (`compile`, `test`, `package`, `install`). `mvn` downloads jars from repositories, runs plugins, and generates sites and reports. It replaced hand-maintained Ant scripts for thousands of libraries and became the backbone of Maven Central.

narrative.whyChosen: Maven brought conventions and dependency management that Ant lacked.
narrative.whyImportant: The POM and Central repository model defined how Java shares libraries to this day.
narrative.problemSolved: Every Java project reinvented directory structure and jar classpath wiring.
